exposure: Sexually transmitted disease (STD) pathogens identified by Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT)
outcome: Prevalence of positive STD tests and specific pathogens (e.g., Ureaplasma parvum, Mycoplasma hominis) via NAAT
Predictive clinical and laboratory parameters for positive NAAT results
cohort: The study participants were 610 women with clinically diagnosed Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) in a secondary referral center whose records were reviewed from 2016 to 2019.
finding: 17% of women with clinically diagnosed PID in the cohort had a positive STD PCR, with Ureaplasma parvum, Mycoplasma hominis, and Ureaplasma urealyticum being the most prevalent pathogens, and a lower prevalence of Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhea was observed compared to other populations.
